messages:
maria: quick heads-up — i opened a follow-up to the SDK pagination/transport RFC. major ask: make pagination semver-safe across py/ts/go without surprise behavior changes

ashok: nice. what do you mean by 'semver-safe' here?

maria: today we sometimes change iterator resume semantics (auto-resume token, implicit retry on transient transport errors) and that causes minor version bumps to break callers. proposal: any change that can alter token shape, resume semantics, or retry-visible behavior must be a minor+ migration and we provide a compatibility shim for 12 months

kevin: +1 on the policy. implementation question: do we add cross-language client-side shim or server-side compatibility layer?

maria: prefer client-side shims because transports differ. server could help but we'd still need SDKs to opt-in to old behavior for safety

tammy: can we be concrete on the shim surface? i.e., new paged interface vs old iterator. suggestion: add a lightweight Cursor object that contains a versioned token and a flag for transport-retry semantics. old iterator wrappers can emit Cursor(v=1, token=...) so older code still works

jules: we should also standardize how retry interacts with pagination. currently some SDKs retry the entire page request (idempotent) and some do resume-from-last-successful-item which hides duplicates. which do we favor?

ashok: leaning towards 'retry entire page' by default for consistency. dedupe/at-least-once semantics are app-level. we can add an opt-in 'resume-granular' mode that preserves item-level resume but is explicitly labeled and semver-protected

kevin: ok. that makes transport layer simpler. for streaming transports (http2/grpc streams) we need a separate flow — maybe Cursor.kind = "stream" vs "paged" so transport knows how to reattach

maria: agreed. added a sketch in the thread README:

```python
# new cursor-first pattern (py)
client.list_items(cursor=Cursor.from_token(token_str))
# explicit resume semantics
client.list_items(cursor=Cursor.from_parts(version=1, kind='paged', token=...))
```

```ts
// ts shape
const cursor = Cursor.parse(tokenStr);
client.listItems({ cursor });
```

```go
// go: Cursor struct with Version, Kind, Raw
cur := sdk.NewCursorFromToken(tok)
client.ListItems(ctx, cur)
```

tammy: + code examples are great. what about default retry policy? if we change default retry behavior that's a breaking change. we should preserve current default and offer a new 'paginationRetryPolicy' config with documented semantics

maria: yes — default stays. new SDK major will expose new defaults; minor will ship opt-in flag with deprecation notice. timeline: 3-phase rollout: 1) publish Cursor type + opt-in flag across SDKs (minor) 2) encourage adoption + console + telemetry (6 months) 3) flip default in next major

jules: telemetry: we need a metric for "token format version in use" and "resume-mode used" so we can measure migration. can infra add tags on requests?

ashok: infra can add header `x-redwood-cursor-v: <n>` on paged calls when Cursor present. we'll forward to logging/tracing

kevin: what about server-side validation? i want servers to return 400 for unknown token versions with a structured error pointing to migration docs, rather than silently accepting and failing later

maria: yes good call. error shape: `{"code":"UNSUPPORTED_CURSOR_VERSION","message":"cursor v3 required","meta":{"supported":"1,2"}}` — documented in API compatibility guide

tammy: migration helpers? maybe a CLI tool to convert token encodings we used historically -> new Cursor envelope for customers running private infra

maria: added a TODO to the follow-up for a small converter library + a node CLI shim. also asked legal about support window for private installs

ci-bot: created issue #3425: "sdk: pagination cursor + semver migration plan" and linked the PR diff (https://git.internal/r/3425) :white_check_mark:

ashok: one more ops question — pagination + retries can increase cost if page size shrinks. we should recommend a default max page size and add a warning metric when clients flip to "resume-granular" mode

jules: +1. docs note: show examples for idempotent vs non-idempotent page handlers. also mention that function-calling/tooling returning dedup keys is helpful

kevin: action items for eng-platform: 1) finalize Cursor spec in the RFC follow-up (maria) 2) add x-redwood-cursor-v header support (ashok) 3) add shim bindings in py/ts/go repos (owners?) 4) telemetry + metrics (jules) 5) docs + migration guide (tammy)

maria: i'll draft the spec today, ping me for reviews. thanks all :rocket:

jules: acked, will add telemetry tickets after we see the initial spec

tammy: i'll start a docs skeleton and paste into the RFC PR

kevin: i'll volunteer to own the ts shim. ashok can you take go?

ashok: yep i can take go.

maria: sweet. closing loop — please add short comments on the issue for any nitpicks. want to keep minor rollout safe and clearly opt-in before any default flips.
